For payment timing — we are trying to avoid a delay into next month. Please advise what you need from our side.

2) Next steps I’m proposing:
- Jonas (tax ops) will confirm whether reverse-charge still applies given the name mismatch and advise invoice wording.
- Neha (billing) will prepare a corrected invoice that prints: net amount, clear reverse-charge line, both vendor and buyer VAT numbers, and an explanation line referencing Article 196.

Subject: RE: Invoice 3891 — VAT ID / reverse-charge mismatch

Thanks all — tax ops notes below. I’ve run the VAT through TaxAssist and a manual check against the German VIES mirror. Findings:

- The VAT number DE123456789 is valid but the VIES record shows the legal name as "Redwood Inference Inc" (our US parent), whereas the certificate Greenfield provided references "Redwood Inference GmbH" in Germany. The discrepancy in vendor legal name causes AP holds even if the VAT number is active.
- Reverse-charge under Article 196 still applies for B2B cross-border electronic services if the buyer is VAT-registered (which Greenfield appears to be). So the tax treatment is likely correct.

Recommended actions to release payment quickly:
1) Billing should reissue invoice 3891 with:
   - Vendor VAT: DE123456789
   - Vendor declared legal name: use the legal name that matches the VIES lookup (Redwood Inference Inc) and add in parentheses our registered EU trading name if applicable ("Redwood Inference (EU ops)").
   - Buyer VAT: DE987654321 (as provided in the certificate)
   - Line: "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under Art. 196 Directive 2006/112/EC"
2) Provide a short cover note confirming Redwood validated the buyer VAT via TaxAssist and that the supply was delivered as hosted software (B2B).
3) Banking details and invoice numbering should be unchanged.

I've attached a quick CSV with the validation log (vat-validation-log.csv). Neha — please generate the corrected invoice and include the cover note Jonas mentions. Lena — once you receive, please confirm if your AP will accept the invoice with the vendor name as shown in VIES; if not, we’ll follow up on adding additional proof (company extract).

If Greenfield still refuses to accept the invoice wording we can escalate to our legal/tax counsel (TaxAssist) and prepare a short joint statement.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Tax Operations — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
